title: NextGen batteries could be transformational | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Simon Flowers, via Wood Mackenzie's EV analyst Milan Thakore, argues the Iran war and high fuel prices could be an inflection point for EVs, with global sales up 14% year-on-year to August and near one in three new cars electric. Chinese exports, fast-charging LFP batteries from end-2026 and a possibly earlier 50% penetration by 2035 are key threads.

insights.claim: Global EV sales including BEV and PHEV rose 14% year-on-year to end August 2026, and EVs now make up nearly one in three new car sales globally.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Global EV adoption continues to grow, but unevenly by region.
insights.quote: EVs now represent nearly one in three new car sales globally.

insights.claim: High fuel prices since the start of the Iran war have driven record September EV penetration in France, the UK, Sweden, Australia, Norway and China, with sales surging in Southeast Asia and Latin America.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Oil price shocks are a demand catalyst for EVs; link fuel price moves to EV equities.

insights.claim: US EV penetration is down after withdrawal of supportive policy, and India is now overtaking the US in percentage terms.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: US EV policy retreat leaves it lagging peers.
insights.quote: The US has still not recovered from the withdrawal of supportive policy and EV penetration is down.

insights.claim: China's EV penetration is approaching 70% yet EV sales are down nearly 1 million units from last year's 9 million peak, because the whole market is shrinking.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Record penetration masks falling volumes; avoid reading penetration as unit growth.
insights.quote: Despite EV penetration approaching 70%, EV sales are down by nearly 1 million units

insights.claim: Chinese light vehicle sales across all powertrains fell 3.6 million units year-on-year, with ICE vehicles taking more than double the hit of EVs due to high fuel costs, fewer legacy replacement buyers and a weaker macro outlook.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: The ICE collapse lifts EV share almost to China's 2030 target four years early.
insights.locator: What's holding EVs back in China?

insights.claim: Chinese EV makers will ramp exports to offset slowing domestic growth, using competitive pricing, such as Leapmotor's B05 at around EUR 30,000, up to a 300-mile range, a comparable German ICE model costing up to EUR 5,000 more.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Chinese price competitiveness pressures European OEM margins; Stellantis-Leapmotor is a channel to track.
insights.locator: Will Chinese EVs manufacturers ramp up exports?

insights.claim: European-made Chinese EVs will eventually replace imports as Chinese automakers build manufacturing capacity and battery supply chains in Europe, forcing European OEMs to keep advancing to protect share.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Localisation blunts tariff and protection strategies; European OEM share risk.
insights.locator: Is Europe about to be swamped by Chinese exports?

insights.claim: Europe has the highest EV penetration outside China, pushing towards 40%, supported by subsidies, model availability and high retail fuel prices.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Europe is the main battleground for Chinese export competition.
insights.locator: Is Europe about to be swamped by Chinese exports?

insights.claim: EV sales in South America and Southeast Asia have all but doubled on a flood of Chinese imports, and East Asian BEV growth has doubled as Hyundai-Kia sells into its home market to offset US demand weakness.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Emerging markets are now the growth outlet for Chinese EV makers.

insights.claim: The latest LFP batteries, pushed by CATL and BYD, reach international markets at the end of 2026 and cut charging from up to 30 minutes to below 10 minutes, requiring charging infrastructure to move from kilowatt to megawatt level.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Winners include battery leaders and megawatt charging suppliers; closes the charging-time gap with ICE refuelling.
insights.quote: These will dramatically speed up charging from up to 30 minutes today to below 10 minutes.

insights.claim: The Iran war may prove an inflection point that accelerates EVs eating into ICE share, driven by improving vehicle quality, range and charging speed plus soaring 2026 gasoline and diesel prices; conflict duration and pump prices will set the pace and road fuel demand erosion.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Structural bearish read on oil road-fuel demand if high prices persist.
insights.quote: Our sense is that the Iran war will be seen as an inflection point
insights.locator: Are we at an inflection point for EVs?

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's base case of 50% global passenger EV penetration by 2035 could arrive a few years earlier.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Upside risk to EV adoption forecasts and downside risk to long-run oil demand.
insights.quote: It’s possible that Wood Mackenzie’s base case assumption that global passenger EV penetration hits 50% by 2035 arrives a few years earlier.
insights.locator: Are we at an inflection point for EVs?
